narrative_purpose: Shows the first generation of stars igniting inside an unenriched cloud, so the reader can picture why the universe stopped being a hydrogen desert within a few million years.
subject: A vast dark cloud of gas filling most of the frame, with five or six intensely bright blue-white points of light ignited inside it at different depths. Each point carves a small clear cavity in the surrounding gas and lights the cloud walls around it from within. No planets, no disks - only the newborn stars and the gas.
scene: Deep space at the earliest epoch: the cloud is smooth, almost featureless, with long faint filaments and no dust lanes or knots of debris. The lit cavities show layered translucent veils of gas receding into darkness.
camera: Wide establishing view from outside the cloud, looking into it, with strong sense of depth from near gas edges to far interior.
light: The newborn stars are the only sources - hard blue-white cores, their glow attenuating quickly into the gas so most of the frame remains very dark; volumetric haze catches the light in shafts.
palette: Void-indigo and deep teal-indigo gas dominating, cool cyan and near-white star cores, one small scarce amber knot at a distance, mist-grey haze in the lit shafts.
style: Painterly atmospheric astronomical plate, layered haze, soft dissolving edges.
detail_level: Low to moderate: the individual stars sharp, the gas broad and soft with painterly texture, deliberately empty of small detail.
composition: The brightest star sits lower left; the others scatter toward the upper right in a loose diagonal. The upper left quadrant is nearly empty dark gas, open for a callout.
consistency_notes: This is the pre-enrichment universe, so the cloud must read as clean and smooth - no rocky debris, no dust knots, no protoplanetary disks anywhere in frame.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no grid, no planets, no protoplanetary disks, no spacecraft, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon glow
